paragraphs.title: The King and the Levites Prepare for Passover

easy.explanation: The text says Josiah kept the Passover unto the LORD in Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where did Josiah keep the Passover?

easy.explanation: The Passover was killed on the fourteenth day of the first month.
easy.q: On what day of the first month was the Passover killed?

answers: Serve in the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: Josiah encouraged the priests to the service of the house of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Josiah encourage the priests to do?

answers: In the house which Solomon built
medium.explanation: They were told to put the holy ark in the house Solomon built.
medium.q: Where did Josiah tell the Levites to put the holy ark?

answers: So the Passover service could be orderly
So they could choose a new king
So they could go to war
medium.explanation: The people were organized according to their ancestral houses and service divisions.
medium.q: Why were the people to prepare by their fathers’ houses and divisions?

medium.explanation: A burden is something carried, especially upon the shoulders.
medium.q: In the phrase “it shall not be a burden upon your shoulders,” what does “burden” mean?

answers: They were to leave their service
They were to serve the LORD and prepare their brethren
They were to command the army
challenge.explanation: Josiah told them to serve the LORD and His people and prepare the Passover.
challenge.q: What practical change did Josiah require of the Levites?

answers: It was carried out without order
It required divisions and assigned duties
It was only the king’s responsibility
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes courses, divisions, families, and specific responsibilities.
challenge.q: What does the arrangement of priests and Levites show about the Passover service?

challenge.explanation: The arrangement followed the writing of David and the writing of Solomon his son.
challenge.q: According to whose writings were the ancestral houses and divisions arranged?

easy.explanation: Josiah gave lambs, kids, and bullocks for the Passover offerings.
easy.q: What did Josiah give to the people?

easy.explanation: Josiah gave thirty thousand animals of the flock.
easy.q: How many animals of the flock did Josiah give for the Passover?

easy.explanation: The priests sprinkled the blood, while the Levites flayed the animals.
easy.q: What did the priests do after the Passover was killed?

answers: Five thousand small cattle and five hundred oxen
Two thousand six hundred small cattle and three hundred oxen
Thirty thousand small cattle and three thousand oxen
medium.explanation: The chief Levites gave five thousand small cattle and five hundred oxen.
medium.q: What did the chief Levites give to the Levites?

answers: The priests were busy offering burnt offerings and the fat
The priests had gone to war
The priests were absent from Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The priests were busy with the offerings until night.
medium.q: Why did the Levites prepare food for the priests?

medium.explanation: Courses were organized groups serving in their assigned order.
medium.q: What does “courses” mean in “the Levites in their courses”?

answers: Each group performed its assigned duty
Josiah performed all the work himself
Only the people handled the offerings
challenge.explanation: The priests sprinkled the blood, the Levites flayed and prepared the offerings, and others remained at their posts.
challenge.q: How is cooperation in the Passover service shown?

answers: The Temple service included varied and regular duties
They were responsible for the army
challenge.explanation: The singers and porters continued their assigned Temple service.
challenge.q: What does the singers’ and porters’ remaining at their posts show?

answers: They supplied animals for the offerings
They were used only for lamentations
challenge.explanation: Their gifts supplied the animals needed for sacrifices and the Passover meal.
challenge.q: How did the officials’ donations help the Passover service?

easy.explanation: They kept the feast seven days.
easy.q: How long did the children of Israel keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread?

answers: The children of Israel that were present
easy.explanation: The text says that the children of Israel who were present kept the Passover.
easy.q: Who kept the Passover at that time?

easy.explanation: This Passover was kept in the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign.
easy.q: In what year of Josiah’s reign was this Passover kept?

medium.explanation: The passage compares it with the days of Samuel the prophet.
medium.q: Since whose days had there not been a Passover like this one?

answers: The priests, Levites, Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem’s inhabitants
medium.explanation: The passage lists the priests, Levites, Judah, Israel that were present, and Jerusalem’s inhabitants.
medium.q: Who is named as participating in this great Passover?

answers: Those who were there at that time
medium.explanation: It refers to the Israelites who were present for the celebration.
medium.q: What does “that were present” mean in this passage?

challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes the exceptional size and importance of Josiah’s Passover.
challenge.q: What does the statement “there was no passover like to that” emphasize?

answers: The organized service made a broad celebration possible
The preparations prevented the people from participating
The preparations had no connection with the feast
challenge.explanation: The orderly work of the priests and Levites supported the large public celebration.
challenge.q: How did the earlier preparations contribute to the great Passover?

answers: It says every Israelite in every land attended
It refers to Israel that was present and the inhabitants of Jerusalem
It says only Josiah’s family attended
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically mentions those present and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What limits the scope of the description of the participants?

paragraphs.title: The Confrontation with Neco and Josiah’s Death

easy.explanation: Neco king of Egypt came up to fight against Charchemish.
easy.q: Who came up to fight against Charchemish?

easy.explanation: Josiah came to fight in the valley of Megiddo, where he was shot.

answers: They left him in the field
easy.explanation: They took him out of the chariot and brought him to Jerusalem.
easy.q: What did Josiah’s servants do after he was wounded?

answers: His war was not against Judah
He had come to celebrate Passover
He wanted to become king of Judah
medium.explanation: Neco said, “I come not against thee this day, but against the house wherewith I have war.”

answers: He disguised himself, refused to turn back, and did not hearken to Neco
He did not know where he was
Neco invited him to a peace meeting
medium.explanation: Josiah disguised himself to fight and did not listen to Neco’s words.
medium.q: Why did Josiah continue toward the battle?

medium.explanation: Josiah disguised himself so that he might fight.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “disguised himself” mean?

answers: The confrontation, Josiah’s wounding, his return to Jerusalem, and his death
Josiah’s death, the confrontation, the Passover, and the lamentations
The lamentations, the wounding, the battle, and a return to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The passage presents these events in that order.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is described?

challenge.explanation: The text says that all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
challenge.q: How did Judah and Jerusalem respond to Josiah’s death?

answers: A great Passover is followed by Josiah’s wounding and death
The Passover was canceled and Josiah became king
The Passover was held in Egypt and Josiah returned to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The great celebration is followed soon afterward by the battle that led to Josiah’s death.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Josiah’s Passover and his death?

paragraphs.title: Laments and the Record of Josiah

easy.explanation: The text says, “And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah.”

answers: The singing men and singing women
easy.explanation: The singing men and singing women spoke of Josiah in their lamentations.
easy.q: Who spoke of Josiah in their lamentations?

answers: In the book of the kings of Israel and Judah
easy.explanation: The passage says his deeds were written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
easy.q: Where were Josiah’s deeds, first and last, written?

medium.explanation: The lamentations were made an ordinance in Israel.
medium.q: What became an ordinance in Israel?

answers: The writings of the officials only
medium.explanation: His goodness was recorded according to what was written in the law of the LORD.
Lamentations are expressions or songs of grief for the dead.

answers: The mourning for Josiah was preserved as a lasting custom
The lamentations were spoken only on the day of his death
challenge.explanation: The lamentations became an established practice in Israel and continued as a remembrance.
challenge.q: What does making the lamentations an ordinance show?

answers: It points to records of both his goodness and his deeds
It cancels the lamentations for him
It describes the beginning of Neco’s reign
challenge.explanation: The summary refers to his goodness and to records of his deeds from first to last.
challenge.q: How does the final summary complete the account of Josiah?

answers: The lamentations express mourning, while the records preserve Josiah’s goodness and deeds
The lamentations describe war, while the records describe only food
They have exactly the same purpose
challenge.explanation: The lamentations express grief, while the written sources document Josiah’s life and actions.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the lamentations and the written records?
